text: A fraction names equal parts of a whole. In 3/4, the denominator 4 means the whole is divided into four equal parts, and the numerator 3 means three parts are selected.
Equivalent fractions have the same value. Multiplying both the numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number preserves the fraction; for example, 2/3 = 4/6.
To compare fractions with a common denominator, compare their numerators. Since 5/8 has more eighths than 3/8, 5/8 is greater than 3/8.
